name: Maya Long Count zero on Uaxactun monuments
description: Maya scribes used explicit zero signs in a calendar count expressed in positional units on monuments at Uaxactun.

date.label: Conventionally dated 357 CE
date.basis: Scholars associate the stelae with the 357 CE period ending represented in the Long Count; this is not an independently measured carving date.

events.statement: Scholars associate Uaxactun Stelae 18 and 19 with a 357 CE period ending; their Long Count inscriptions include explicit zero signs.

evidence.supports: The 2021 study interprets explicit zero signs in the Long Count on Uaxactun Stelae 18 and 19 dated to 357 CE.
The authors interpret the monuments as dedicated at the 357 period ending.

contributions.group: Maya scribes of the Uaxactun monuments
contributions.resource: Recorded Long Count dates with explicit zero glyphs.

evidence.supports: Scholars describe zero glyphs in Uaxactun’s 357 CE Long Count inscriptions.

earliest_record.rationale: Scholarly association of dedication with the represented date, not an exact carving date or claim of the origin of zero.

caveats: The represented date is an epigraphic date associated with the monuments; it does not independently establish the origin of zero or the exact carving day. The Long Count is mixed-radix, not pure base 20; earlier Mesoamerican counts do not by themselves show an explicit zero glyph.
